newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian fuel prices increased by 15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Zambian fuel prices increased by 15 percent.

text.p: Zambia on Tuesday hiked fuel prices by 15 percent in response to the weakening local currency and an increase in international prices.
"The prices of gas oil, premium and domestic kerosene have been adjusted upward by 15 percent," a Zambia National Oil Company spokesman said.
As a result, petrol would cost 786 kwacha (US$0.59) a litre, diesel 735 kwacha ($0.55) and paraffin 405 kwacha ($0.31).
The increase is the third this year, having last been raised in April by 11 percent.
Zambia has suffered fuel shortages for most of the year following maintenance closures at the state-run oil refinery and at the port of Dar-es-Salaam in neighbouring Tanzania.
Zambia had to import finished petroleum products from its neighbours during the maintenance closures.
